method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from ASHM Health 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens' (DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023)), 24 claims; LICENCE: © ASHM, Australia, 2026 (site footer only; no reuse terms: the footer's Copyright & Disclaimer link returned 404 on 2026-09-23) (read at site footer of https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/ (read 2026-09-23)). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Initial Regimens: ART-naive Adults; Switch Strategies for Virologically Suppressed Persons' (version 13.0, 2025 (web pages read 2026-09-24)), 12 claims; LICENCE: © EACS, 2026 - All Rights Reserved (page footer); EACS permits downloading the guidelines for own use and reproducing a portion for educational purposes with referencing (read at the page footers of the two eacs.sanfordguide.com pages and the EACS guidelines page (https://www.eacsociety.org/guidelines/eacs-guidelines/)). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2, the European AIDS Clinical Society guidelines v13.0 (2025): the initial-regimens and switch-strategies pages of the web edition (https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-initial-regimens-arv-naive-adults and https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-switch-strategies), saved together as one text file; every S1 claim is unchanged. EACS v13.0 is published only on the web (no PDF). S2 is all-rights-reserved, so it is paraphrased and hash-anchored.

claims.claim: **Everyone with HIV should be offered ART,** both to cut HIV-related illness and death and to stop transmission to partners and infants (AI). **Start it as soon as possible after diagnosis** (AII).
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **(AU) Whether same-day starts improve long-term engagement and viral suppression is not known.** Timing is decided jointly by prescriber and patient; link a patient who is unsure to peer-based programmes.
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Make clear that ART does not cure HIV** and has to be taken indefinitely without breaks to keep immune function and viral suppression.
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Early ART matters most in AIDS-defining illness, acute or recent infection, and pregnancy,** where delay carries high risks of illness, death and transmission.
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **(AU) Late diagnosis is common: 48% of Australian HIV notifications in 2021 were late,** the highest share in 10 years.
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **With an acute opportunistic infection, start ART,** but for cryptococcal or TB meningitis a short delay may be justified because immediate ART raises the risk of serious IRIS. In non-meningeal TB, starting ART during TB treatment gives a clear survival benefit.
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A cancer diagnosis should not hold up ART, and starting ART should not hold up cancer treatment.**
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Resistance genotype before treatment:** in people never exposed to ARVs, test reverse transcriptase and protease genes; add integrase testing when transmitted INSTI resistance is a concern.
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do a pregnancy test before starting ART,** and ask everyone who could become pregnant about their plans.
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **(AU) Screen for HLA-B*5701 before any abacavir-containing regimen (AI).** A positive result means no abacavir, recorded in the notes as an abacavir allergy, because the hypersensitivity risk is above 50%. The test is available across Australia as a targeted genetic test without full HLA typing.
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **HLA-B*5701 needs testing only once in a lifetime,** so record the result carefully. A negative result does not completely exclude abacavir hypersensitivity.
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For most people, start an oral second-generation INSTI with two NRTIs:** bictegravir/TAF/emtricitabine (AI), or dolutegravir with TAF/emtricitabine, TDF/emtricitabine or TDF/lamivudine (AI). Dolutegravir/lamivudine as a two-drug regimen suits some people (AI).
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid dolutegravir/lamivudine when the viral load is above 500,000 copies/mL, with hepatitis B co-infection, or before the genotype and HBV results are back.**
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **After long-acting cabotegravir PrEP, do not start an INSTI until an INSTI genotype shows no resistance;** if ART must start first, use boosted darunavir with TAF or TDF plus emtricitabine or lamivudine (AIII). **(AU)** Cabotegravir PrEP was TGA-approved in 2022 but its PBS listing process ceased by June 2024, though some patients may have used it overseas; request an integrase genotype.
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If viral suppression has not been reached 8 to 12 weeks into an INSTI regimen, repeat resistance testing, including integrase.**
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dolutegravir/abacavir/lamivudine is now a second-tier option,** because abacavir needs an HLA-B*5701 test, carries a possible cardiovascular risk, and other choices exist. Use it (BI) when kidney or bone concerns rule out TAF and TDF, only in documented HLA-B*5701-negative people, and not in hepatitis B co-infection unless another HBV-active drug such as entecavir is added.
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Boosted darunavir is the one protease inhibitor recommended to start with, and only in certain situations.** Transmitted PI resistance is uncommon, so it is favoured over an NNRTI when starting before resistance results, and its high resistance barrier suits people at risk of patchy adherence.
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **In pregnancy use ritonavir-boosted darunavir, not cobicistat-boosted:** cobicistat regimens give inadequate drug levels in pregnancy and should not be started. Dolutegravir is now the preferred INSTI in pregnancy, since updated data showed no significant excess of neural tube defects.
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Kidney function limits cobicistat-boosted darunavir:** with TDF/emtricitabine it is not recommended below a creatinine clearance of 70 mL/min, and with TAF/emtricitabine not below 30 mL/min.
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Darunavir contains a sulfonamide group; use it cautiously in severe sulfonamide allergy,** though most people with that allergy tolerate it.
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Separate dolutegravir from cation antacids and laxatives:** give it 2 hours or more ahead of them, or wait 6 hours or more afterwards.
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tenofovir-free regimens should not be used with hepatitis B co-infection unless an HBV-active drug such as entecavir is added.**
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Weight gain on INSTI- or TAF-based regimens is not a reason to withhold them.**
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **(AU) Doravirine/TDF/lamivudine is TGA-approved but not PBS-reimbursed.**
claims.locator: ASHM Health, 'HIV Management Guidelines: Antiretroviral Guidelines (US DHHS Adult and Adolescent guidelines with Australian commentary): Initial Combination ARV Regimens; Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy; HLA-B*5701 Screening; Protease Inhibitor-Based Regimens; INSTI-Based Regimens', DHHS text last updated September 2024 (initiation section December 2019); Australian commentary last updated December 2024 (initiation and HLA-B*5701 July 2023), https://hiv.guidelines.org.au/arv-adult/what-start/intro/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **EACS recommended first regimens:** bictegravir/TAF/emtricitabine; dolutegravir with TAF/emtricitabine or TDF with emtricitabine or lamivudine; dolutegravir/lamivudine when HBsAg-negative with viral load under 500,000 copies/mL (not after suspected PrEP failure); or doravirine with TAF/emtricitabine or TDF with emtricitabine or lamivudine.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Initial Regimens: ART-naive Adults; Switch Strategies for Virologically Suppressed Persons', version 13.0, 2025 (web pages read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-initial-regimens-arv-naive-adults, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **EACS alternatives:** abacavir/lamivudine/dolutegravir (HLA-B*57:01- and HBsAg-negative); raltegravir, efavirenz (at bedtime or 2 hours before dinner) or rilpivirine (only with CD4 over 200 cells/μL, viral load under 100,000 copies/mL, no acid-reducing drugs, and with food) with two NRTIs; or boosted darunavir with two NRTIs, taken with food.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Initial Regimens: ART-naive Adults; Switch Strategies for Virologically Suppressed Persons', version 13.0, 2025 (web pages read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-initial-regimens-arv-naive-adults, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **HIV acquired while taking oral TDF/FTC PrEP: move straight to three drugs,** a high-barrier third agent (dolutegravir or bictegravir, or else boosted darunavir) with tenofovir and emtricitabine or lamivudine, without a gap in treatment. After any PrEP failure, avoid a two-drug start unless the genotype shows no resistance.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Initial Regimens: ART-naive Adults; Switch Strategies for Virologically Suppressed Persons', version 13.0, 2025 (web pages read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-initial-regimens-arv-naive-adults, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Doravirine cautions (EACS):** it has no activity against HIV-2, has been compared with efavirenz and darunavir but not with an INSTI, is unsuitable for a rapid start, and a resistance genotype is advisable before it is used.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Initial Regimens: ART-naive Adults; Switch Strategies for Virologically Suppressed Persons', version 13.0, 2025 (web pages read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-initial-regimens-arv-naive-adults, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Doses from EACS:** TAF 10 mg alongside P-gp inhibitors and 25 mg otherwise; raltegravir 400 mg twice daily or 1200 mg (two 600 mg tablets) once daily, but twice daily with inducers such as TB drugs or antiepileptics, or with calcium, magnesium or iron; efavirenz 400 or 600 mg daily, and 600 mg with a rifampicin-based TB regimen.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Initial Regimens: ART-naive Adults; Switch Strategies for Virologically Suppressed Persons', version 13.0, 2025 (web pages read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-initial-regimens-arv-naive-adults, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Choose TAF first over TDF** in established chronic kidney disease or high CKD risk, with nephrotoxic co-medication or past TDF toxicity, and in osteoporosis, progressive osteopenia, a high FRAX score or a past fragility fracture. In some countries TDF 300 mg is labelled 245 mg (the prodrug content); the salts are interchangeable.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Initial Regimens: ART-naive Adults; Switch Strategies for Virologically Suppressed Persons', version 13.0, 2025 (web pages read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-initial-regimens-arv-naive-adults, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **'Suppressed' in switch trials means a viral load under 50 copies/mL held for 6 months or longer.** Before any switch, review the whole ARV history, viral loads, tolerability and cumulative resistance; the aim is to keep suppression while fixing side effects, interactions or comorbidity problems.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Initial Regimens: ART-naive Adults; Switch Strategies for Virologically Suppressed Persons', version 13.0, 2025 (web pages read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-initial-regimens-arv-naive-adults, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Switches within a class, or between drugs with the same resistance barrier, are usually safe without resistance.** Dolutegravir- and bictegravir-based triple regimens can be used even when the two NRTIs are not fully active, but a boosted PI can go to an NNRTI or raltegravir only if both NRTIs are fully active.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Initial Regimens: ART-naive Adults; Switch Strategies for Virologically Suppressed Persons', version 13.0, 2025 (web pages read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-initial-regimens-arv-naive-adults, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **If a switch stops TDF without starting TAF, check hepatitis B status and vaccination first;** in chronic hepatitis B, keep TDF or TAF unless another HBV drug such as entecavir is used. See the person about 4 weeks after any switch.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Initial Regimens: ART-naive Adults; Switch Strategies for Virologically Suppressed Persons', version 13.0, 2025 (web pages read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-initial-regimens-arv-naive-adults, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Oral two-drug maintenance** (dolutegravir/rilpivirine, lamivudine/dolutegravir, or emtricitabine or lamivudine with boosted darunavir) is only for people suppressed below 50 copies/mL for 6 months, with no past resistance and with hepatitis B immunity.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Initial Regimens: ART-naive Adults; Switch Strategies for Virologically Suppressed Persons', version 13.0, 2025 (web pages read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-initial-regimens-arv-naive-adults, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Long-acting cabotegravir + rilpivirine injections:** start on the day of the last oral pills (an oral lead-in month is optional) with CAB 600 mg/RPV 900 mg on day 0 and at month 1, then every 2 months. Failure and resistance are more likely when several of these coexist: archived rilpivirine mutations, HIV subtype A6, and a BMI of 30 or more (use a longer needle).
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Initial Regimens: ART-naive Adults; Switch Strategies for Virologically Suppressed Persons', version 13.0, 2025 (web pages read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-initial-regimens-arv-naive-adults, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Not recommended:** monotherapy, NRTI-only combinations, other two-drug pairings, and planned or prolonged treatment interruptions. Four-days-a-week triple therapy looked non-inferior in one trial but is not yet for routine use. A well-tolerated older regimen does not need changing just because it is no longer preferred.
claims.locator: European AIDS Clinical Society (EACS), web edition hosted by Sanford Guide, 'EACS Guidelines version 13.0: Initial Regimens: ART-naive Adults; Switch Strategies for Virologically Suppressed Persons', version 13.0, 2025 (web pages read 2026-09-24), https://eacs.sanfordguide.com/eacs-part1/art/eacs-initial-regimens-arv-naive-adults, retrieved 2026-09-24
